matches.note: Berwick-on-Tweed pier-head lights.
Findlay prints 'FARN ISLAND'; the high and low lights are both in this one row.

The row's name is blank. It continues the Tees entries after South Gare (p61r21). Its item 2, 'Fifth buoy, fix. red lt.' at 54 37.6 N 1 10.5 W, is the No. 5 Buoy light. Findlay doesn't call it a light-vessel, and the same row also holds the Fourth buoy and Seal Sand lights.

Kind 'other'. This is a second 1880 return from Teesmouth, at the same map point as the No. 5 Buoy L.V. (44_a/44_b). It may be a shore observer. If it is a second return from the Tees lights, the row would be p61r22.
'South Gare Breakwater', established 1884, which fits the reports (1885-86).
Findlay prints 'HIGH WHITBY': two lights (the north and south towers on Ling Hill) in one row.
The lighthouse: high and low lights in one row at 53 34.7 N 0 7.2 E.
'Spurn Lightvessel', 'off the point', at 0 13 E (east of the lighthouse). This is the Newsand light-vessel.
'Bull Sand Lightvessel ... off Spurn Point'. The latitude reads 53 54, which must be wrong: it should be about 53 34.
Kind 'other'. Great Coates is an inland observer's place on the Humber near Grimsby, and Findlay has no light there.
Not the Lynn Channel light-vessel (p60r17), which lies 8 miles further in.
Kind 'other'. Northrepps is an inland village near Cromer with no light.
Findlay prints 'HASBOROUGH', a single occulting light (altered 1884). The light-vessel is in the next row.
'HASBOROUGH LT.-VES.', near the north end of the sand. Not the Would light-vessel (p60r9) off its south end.
'WINTERTON NESS'.
High and low lights in one row. Lowestoft Harbour (p60r1) is a separate set of pier lights.
Two lights in one row.
Findlay prints 'GOODWIN LT.-VESSEL', 'off North end of the Goodwin Sands', which is the North Sand Head vessel.
The reports' 'East Side'. Findlay: 'about 1½ mile to the eastward of the Goodwin Sands'.
High and low electric lights in one row.
'R. SOVEREIGN SHOALS', described as a 'Lt.-vessel' in the description.
Channel Islands, not in the England extract. Findlay 1887 does list the Casquets, probably in the section with France or the Channel Islands. This null only means 'not in this table'.
Guernsey, not in the England extract. It is certainly in Findlay elsewhere (see Casquets).
Not in the England extract. Heligoland was British until 1890, but its lighthouse would be printed under Germany or the North Sea, so look for it in that section.
Kind 'other', despite 'L.H.' in the print. Findlay has no light at Allonby. The nearest are Maryport (p58r16), the Solway Lightvessel (p58r17) and Lee Scar/Skinburness (p58r18-19).
The offshore vessel 14¾ miles off Walney. Not the Grange Channel light-vessel (p58r4).

No 'Point of Air' row is in the table. Row p57r10 is missing from the sequence, between River Dee Lightvessel (p57r9) and N.W. Lightship (p57r11), which is exactly where Point of Air would fall in coast order. It was almost certainly lost in transcription, so check the scan. The likely answer is p57r10.
'MENAI, TRWYN-DU PT.'
Item 1 of the 'Holyhead' row: the lighthouse on the breakwater.
A fog-signal station, not a light. Findlay has no North Stack row.
'ST. TUDWALL ROADS'.
No position is printed. The row describes leading lights inside Milford Haven.
Findlay prints the high and low lights together ('MILFORD HAVEN ST. ANN'S POINT'). This row is shared with st-anns-head-high and st-anns-head.
The same row as the low light.
Both Nash towers are in one row, so this row is shared with nash-point-high.
'Usk (Newport)', the white tower on the west side.
'Avon': the 1840 white tower at the river mouth. The 'Avonmouth' row (p55r7) is a pair of 1880 leading lights through King Road, not the keepers' lighthouse.
'Burnham, or Bridgewater': upper and lower lights in one row.
'BIDEFORD': two lights on Braunton Sands.
A fog-gun station, not a light, and it has no row of its own. Its position could be taken from the Lundy row (p54r16).
Findlay prints 'SCILLY', the tower on St. Agnes Island.
Two towers in one row.
Item 1 of 'FALMOUTH': the lighthouse on St. Anthony Point.
The Devon Start Point (50 13.3 N 3 38.5 W). The Orkney one is not in this table.
'PORTLAND': two towers near the Bill in one row. Not Portland Breakwater (p53r9).
Findlay prints 'DURLSTON HEAD', the lighthouse 'on Anvil Point' (1881).
Findlay prints 'Hurst Beach': two towers in the rear of the fortifications.
'NEEDLES OUTER ROCK'.
The Isle of Man Point of Ayre (54 24.9 N 4 22 W), not the Flintshire Point of Air.
'DOUGLAS', the tower on Douglas Head. Not Douglas Harbour or Douglas Bay (p59r9-10).
Established 1880, which fits the reports from 1880. One report prints it 'L.V.', which is a slip.

notes:
Things to check:
1. Missing rows in findlay1887_ENGLAND.csv: p52r20, p57r10, p61r1 and p61r19 are absent from the sequence. p57r10 almost certainly holds Point of Air (Flintshire), so point-of-ayr-wales is null only because the row is missing. Check the scan and re-transcribe. p61r19 sits between Whitby Harbour and Coatham, and may be the heading of the Tees entries (see 3).
2. Bull Sand Lightvessel (p61r4) is printed or transcribed at lat 53 54. It should be about 53 34 (off Spurn), so fix it before using the position.
3. p61r22 has a blank name. It continues the Tees entries (Fourth buoy, Fifth buoy, Seal Sand), and I matched the Tees No. 5 Buoy L.V. to its item 2. Findlay calls it a buoy light, not a light-vessel, so check whether it was a vessel in 1887.
4. Casquets, Hanois and Heligoland are not in this England extract, though Findlay 1887 lists them elsewhere (the Channel Islands probably with France, Heligoland with Germany or the North Sea). Their nulls mean 'not in this table', not 'not in Findlay'.
5. Shared rows (one Findlay row for several stations): p56r4 for st-anns-head-low, st-anns-head-high and st-anns-head; p55r14 for nash-point-low and nash-point-high. No station needed extra_rows: every high/low pair here is printed in a single row (Spurn, Whitby, Farn, South Foreland, Lizard, Portland, Hurst, Orfordness, Lowestoft, Nash, St Ann's, Bideford, Burnham).
6. The 'other' stations without a light (Great Cotes, Northrepps, Allonby, North Stack fog signal, Lundy fog gun, the 1880 second Teesmouth) are null. If you want positions for them, the nearest rows are given in their notes.
7. Several rows match one item of a multi-item entry, so the character and position should be taken from that item only: Holyhead Breakwater = item 1 of p56r20, St Anthony = item 1 of p54r2 'FALMOUTH', Tees = item 2 of p61r22.
